name: Lip liner overlining

lead: Overlining means tracing a lip pencil a little beyond the natural lip edge so lips look larger. It is a standard makeup technique, and makeup artists describe it as a way to suggest volume without procedures.
No studies measure how much it changes perceived lip size or attractiveness.

paras: The pencil extends the visible lip border and gives a sharper contrast with the surrounding skin, which can make the lips look more prominent.

Pencils are removable, but allergic contact dermatitis to lip product ingredients has been reported. Permanent lip-liner tattoos are a separate practice with documented complications and difficult removal.

lead: Overlining is a makeup technique in which a lip liner pencil is drawn slightly outside the natural lip border, and the space is filled with lip color, to create the appearance of fuller or larger lips [1][2]. Wikipedia's article on lip liner describes this effect without using the term, noting that liner sharpens the boundary between lips and skin so that lips look more prominent [1].

Lip liner itself is a firmer, more heavily pigmented relative of lipstick, containing more wax and less oil, and has been used since the 1920s [1]. Makeup guidance summarized in an AI-generated encyclopedia describes overlining as a non-invasive way to suggest volume for people with thinner lips [2].

No clinical studies of overlining's effect on perceived lip size or attractiveness were found. The medical literature touching on lip liners concerns allergic reactions to liner ingredients and the removal of permanent lip-liner tattoos, which is a different practice.
infobox: Appearance of fuller or wider lips
Yes, with makeup removal (unlike lip-liner tattoos)

paras: Lip liner comes as a sharpenable or retractable pencil, usually in shades matched to lipsticks, and is used to even out the outer edge of the lips, stop lipstick from bleeding into surrounding lines, or fill the whole lip as a base [1]. In overlining the line is placed just beyond the natural edge. Makeup advice summarized by Grokipedia suggests choosing a liner one to two shades darker than the lipstick, or slightly darker than the natural lip color for nude looks, and that overlining the corners can make the mouth look wider [2].

The same source states that liner can correct minor asymmetry such as an uneven Cupid's bow and reduce the look of fine lines around the mouth for mature skin [2]. These are claims from makeup practice, not outcomes tested in studies.

Liner pencils have been used since the 1920s, with Clara Bow, Marlene Dietrich and Marilyn Monroe among early adopters, and dark brown liner worn with lighter lipstick became popular in the 1990s [1]. Grokipedia further traces the dark-liner-with-gloss look to Black and Mexican-American chola communities and credits figures such as Lil' Kim with bringing it to mainstream visibility; this account comes from an AI-generated source [2].

Contact allergy has been reported to ingredients in lip products. A case from 1993 described allergic contact dermatitis of the lip margins from para-tertiary-butylphenol in a lip liner [3], and a 2024 systematic review examined allergic contact dermatitis to lip care cosmetic products [4].

Separate from pencil overlining, permanent lip-liner tattoos have been associated with complications including pseudolymphoma at a semi-permanent lip-liner tattoo [5], and reviews describe that removal can be complicated, with some pigments changing color under laser treatment [6][7][8].

No studies found on overlining as a technique. Related published work concerns allergic reactions to lip liner ingredients [3][4] and complications and laser removal of cosmetic lip-liner tattoos [5][6][7][8].

timeline.event: Lip liner pencils come into use [1].
